sourceInformation.tech: Three.js 0.180.0 (R180), WebGPU with WebGL2 fallback, Rapier 0.19.3, Gamepad API, Web Audio API, AI Hub session bridge, PeerJS 1.5.5 / WebRTC
sourceInformation.artDirection: Procedural cel-shaded geometry, ink silhouettes, paper grain and a coral / mint rooftop theatre
sourceInformation.animation: Three.js AnimationMixer and native keyframe clips for the bomber, buckets and bunting; procedural physics and particles
sourceInformation.audio: Code-written swing soundtrack, synthesized sound effects and Animalese-style gibberish; music defaults to 10%
sourceInformation.online: Shared-world co-op: AI Hub 1–4 seats; standalone two-player WebRTC rooms; local couch co-op
sourceInformation.testing: Headless Chromium: complete five-round playthrough, keyboard / mouse / emulated standard gamepad / touch, offline audio waveform checks, real two-page WebRTC rooms, and all four AI Hub harness scenarios; 1920×1080 and portrait visual captures. Physical controllers, real phones, audible listening and external NAT traversal: unknown.
sourceInformation.research: none; native model knowledge. Linked AI Hub implementation read directly for required integration

testingFeedback: Testing caught 8 issues: offline audio initialization, two visual defects, invalid mouse coordinates, online seat IDs, missing Hub tags, a Rapier sensor crash and split-bomb AI targeting. All were fixed.
4 critical issues: invalid mouse coordinates, unusable online seat mapping, missing required Hub metadata and the Rapier runtime crash.
The scripted physics and five-round suite: repeated catches and misses exposed the Rapier trap, and the complete run exposed split-bomb AI targeting. Both now pass through victory.
Headless WebGPU screenshots were least useful because this host can return a blank canvas. Runtime checks verified WebGPU; WebGL captures verified composition.
engineFeedback: Three.js native animation clips and node materials made the illustrated stage and expressive characters straightforward.

I initially passed a pointer-coordinate object as a number and assumed bucket sensors would be harmless. Integration tests corrected the input contract; repeated physics cleanup exposed a sensor failure, so catching uses a swept crossing test while Rapier drives the bombs.
The catching rules, pacing, menu focus, procedural sound and shared-world multiplayer state.
Coordinating WebGPU material compilation, physics stepping and responsive framing in a single-file build.
A simpler built-in workflow for toon shading with WebGPU.
promptFeedback: The source, controller-first design and full vertical-slice requirement gave the game a clear identity.
The no-research rule and required linked multiplayer documentation needed an interpretation: the linked implementation was read directly.
Making the complete arcade loop, four-seat hub support and standalone online play fit a polished single-file game.
Specify whether standalone online play may rely on a public signaling service.

aiHub.name: Kapop
aiHub.tagline: One crook. Three buckets. A sky full of trouble.
aiHub.description: An ink-and-paper rooftop catching caper inspired by Kaboom! Chase the bomber through five escalating rounds, catch golden bombs and rescue your streak with a charged splash, alone or with your bucket brigade.
aiHub.controls: Move: left stick / D-pad, A D or arrow keys, mouse, or touch drag. Splash: Cross / A, Space, click or second touch. Pause: Options / Menu or Esc. Couch P2: arrows / second pad.
